I want to upvote this. The prose was fine, the dialogue wasn't distracting, the story was clean and escalated in a way that made sense, and the anomaly itself was easy to understand without being reductive.

My problem is with the dealing of Dr Schrag's AroAce-ness. While the statements made by the director are clearly meant to illustrate how bad he is, the erasure of her orientation is portrayed as a mere fact of the anomaly, and I agree with Nagiros's request for a content warning. You could do an out of universe warning like with TTSR, or Montauk House, but I think you could put it in the initial RAISA outline and it'd serve its purpose as an in-universe warning without disrupting the narrative in any way.

Currently a novote; I'll upvote once you add a content warning to the beginning.

item.content:encoded:
Approved; no significant risks, significant potential rewards, and all that newfangled identity stuff everyone keeps going on about can actually be a help for a change. —Site Director Wakefield

Dr. Werckman, this experiment was a failure. I am not and never have been asexual or aromantic. SCP-5217-1 showed me that, she showed me… so many things…

As for Dr. Arya Schrag, I'm sure she'll continue to fit right in with her reading group, and spend a lot of quality time with her friends before too long. Tell you what, I'll cancel that talk so she doesn't have to, and I guarantee she'll never think about it again. After all, what's a two-hour webinar compared to some sweet sweet lesbian lovemaking?

Can you consider putting a content warning somewhere, please? This hits deep on a lot of trauma I have as an ace and I didn't expect to get hit by an emotional train while reading.

item.title: Filthy cold-posting scum hooray
item.content:encoded:
I had this idea in July when I read SCP-1423 and saw a photo a former classmate posted on the same day (not the one in the article, for licensing reasons). It just wouldn't get out of my head, so I decided to flesh it out fully, then to work to make it unique, then to put it in Wikidot format in a sandbox. Figured I might as well cold-post it and see if it sinks or swims.

I don't know if this story continues or not, but if it does, I'm sure that it happens in the Academics version of War on All Fronts. But this won't even survive 24 hours so it's pretty silly to think that'll happen.

Lots of people to thank, first among them my friend Alice for drawing the sketch at the end. Next up is RJB_R for writing the SCP that inspired this, even if it has evolved quite a bit since then. Then qntm, who gets a shoutout through Site 41 in the article, for being so dang cool. Also thanks to the people who made the Wiki Syntax guide (I stole all your code no regrets!) and the people who wrote the How to Write an SCP guide for saying that sentient beings have to be Euclid and Foundation personnel aren't stupid. Breaking rules is fun if you're clever about it and don't care about the result!

Have a great day and a great life, and if you upvote, a good month as well!
